title: NBC 2016 — residential dwellings (working transcription)
jurisdiction: India. National code; local development-control rules prevail wherever they are stricter.
basis: A working transcription made as a starting point, not a certification. The architect of record owns this file: verify every figure and citation against the published National Building Code of India 2016 and the local byelaws before relying on any of it. Where the code has sub-cases the importer cannot yet tell apart, this file applies the smallest figure in the ladder — the one that is never a false alarm — and says so in the rule's note.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — habitable rooms
rules.note: Where a dwelling has two habitable rooms the code lets the second be 7.5 m2. This file applies the single-room figure to every habitable room, which over-asks in that case — an architect reviewing the finding decides, not this check.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — habitable rooms
rules.note: Width here is the diameter of the largest circle the finished room can contain: an L-shaped room passes if its main body is wide enough.

The code's ladder: 4.5 m2 with a separate store, 5.0 m2 with a separate dining space, 7.5 m2 where the kitchen is also the dining room. The importer cannot tell which case a plan is, so this file applies the 4.5 m2 floor.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — bathrooms and water-closets
rules.note: The code's ladder: WC alone 1.1 m2 (0.9 m wide), bathroom 1.8 m2 (1.2 m wide), combined 2.8 m2. The classifier labels all three 'bathroom', so this file applies the WC floor. Split this rule when the classifier can tell them apart.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — bathrooms and water-closets
rules.note: The WC-alone floor, for the same reason as sanitary-area.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — store room
NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3 — internal passage within a dwelling
rules.note: 0.9 m is the figure for a passage inside one dwelling. A common corridor serving more than one dwelling needs 1.0 m or more under Part 4 — raise this when the building is not a single house.
Applied to every door with the outside, or an outdoor space, on one side.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — doorway widths
rules.note: Doors serving bathrooms and stores may be narrower. Door rules are matched in file order and the first match wins, so this must stay above internal-door.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3, cl. 12 — doorway widths
NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 4 — means of egress
rules.note: Reachability only: every room of these kinds must reach a door to the outside through door openings on the primary storey. Doors into outdoor spaces count as exits; stairs are not modelled, so a storey with no exterior door reports that fact rather than guessing.

rules.cite: NBC 2016 Vol. 1, Part 3 — openings for light and ventilation, one-tenth of floor area
rules.note: Counts windows and doors to the open air, using width x height. The importer does not yet detect windows, so on current models every room reports as unmeasured rather than passing silently. The rule sits ready for the day the importer does.
